findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The change does what the ticket asks. `ticketContractNodes` drops only the exact top-level `## Work Log` section. The section ends at the next level-1 or level-2 heading. Metadata filtering is unchanged, and the identity format is unchanged. The new integration tests run through the real CLI review/status path with the private reviewer stub, and they would catch a broken implementation. With the old code, appending a Work Log changes the body hash and the review goes stale, so the retention test fails. The Decisions-after-Work-Log test fails if exclusion runs past the next level-2 heading. The scope-edit and phase-only controls are still in place. I found no blocking errors. A few cases the ticket promises are not tested, and the plugin hash files can't be checked from this packet.

No test covers the ticket's promise that nonstandard headings stay bound. Examples: `### Work Log`, `## Work log`, `## Work Log (notes)`, or a Work Log heading containing inline formatting. The current exact-match check on `headingText(node) === 'Work Log'` at depth 2 handles these correctly. But a later change that loosened the match, for example to case-insensitive or prefix matching, would pass every named test. Add one negative control that edits under a level-3 or differently cased Work Log heading and expects the review to go stale.

`headingText` joins raw child values without normalizing them. The match therefore depends on parser trimming and treats inline formatting oddly. For example, ``## `Work Log` `` (inline code) is excluded as standard, while `## Work  Log` (double space) stays bound. This is consistent with 'nonstandard stays bound', except for the inline-code case, which is a slightly broader exclusion than the ticket's 'exact level-2 Work Log heading'. Low risk, but it could be made explicit.

Trust boundary: edits inside the Work Log no longer make the review stale, yet the full ticket, Work Log included, is still sent to later reviewers as context. Someone could put scope-like statements in the log that later reviewers read without the earlier approval being invalidated. The ticket explicitly accepts this ('entries are history, not authority'), so it is not blocking. Consider adding a reviewer-facing note that Work Log content is non-authoritative.

`plugin/inventory.json` and `plugin/identity.json` contain regenerated hashes, presumably from rebuilding `runtime/cli.js`. I can't check them against the bundle bytes from this packet. The native-runtime tests in `execution-upstream-planning-context.test.ts` exercise the copied plugin and would show up any mismatch between the bundle and the inventory.

As the ticket notes, existing approvals whose tickets already contain Work Log content will go stale once after upgrade, because the identity version stays `version: 1` but the body content changes. Nothing silently re-approves them, which is the conservative and intended behaviour.
